- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative or mildly bearish (especially after recent spikes), as models tend to ignore downside risk.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive or bullish, especially if recent prices are rising — models overreact to momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp upward spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment turns neutral or slightly negative.
- Lag in downward corrections: if sentiment turns bearish, delay price drop by 1–2 days in forecast unless confirmed by new data.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >15% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 2–5% if sentiment is neutral or slightly bearish.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate if sentiment is volatile — use 20-day moving average as a sanity check.
- Avoid “sentiment echo”: if sentiment is negative but price is rising, don’t assume continuation — adjust downward 3–5% unless confirmed by technicals.
